plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped pinkish-lilac flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-like leaves appear the following spring and die back by early summer. All parts of the plant are highly toxic.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to Europe, including the UK, France and Germany; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Asia
plants.funFact: Colchicum is the source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling. It is sometimes called 'naked ladies' because the flowers appear without leaves.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, bushy perennial wildflower with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in moist meadows, roadsides and prairies, and is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to Alabama and west to the Rocky Mountains; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies depend heavily on New England asters for fuel during their autumn migration to Mexico, and the timing of the bloom often coincides with their passage.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with strappy leaves and sturdy stems topped with umbels of narrow-petaled, wavy-edged pink flowers that shimmer with a glittering surface. It prefers sunny, well-drained positions and blooms as days shorten.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Drakensberg mountains of South Africa; widely grown in gardens of the UK, Europe and the Pacific coast of North America
plants.funFact: The petals have a sparkling, diamond-dust appearance, which is why nerines are sometimes called 'diamond lilies'. They bloom best when bulbs are crowded and baked by summer sun.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting streets and parks with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (late September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; famous in Pretoria (South Africa), Sydney and Brisbane (Australia), and Buenos Aires (Argentina)
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', thousands of trees bloom in spring, and in Australia a folk belief holds that a jacaranda blossom falling on your head brings good luck.
